text:
Avery: Heads up — after the 17:45 canary deploy we saw a 20-35ms median bump on SSE streaming for /v1/chat/stream when tool-calls are present. Repro on 2 canary hosts. :frowning:
Nia: saw that in the perf dashboard too. p95 went from ~55ms -> ~86ms for the canary group.
Omar: CI perf run earlier this morning also flagged a serialization regression in the proto layer, same timeframe.
Kai: any obvious PRs in the window (17:30-17:50) touching streaming framing, proto marshalling, or batcher heuristics?
Avery: candidates: merge 5d3f9a -> a1b2c7 which introduced a "unified toolcall envelope" and also a small change to kernel cost query in the runtime selector.
BenchBot: perf snapshot (canary hosts):
  - stream_p50_ms: 48 -> 72
  - stream_p95_ms: 56 -> 92
  - serialize_median_ms: 4.8 -> 16.7
  - kvcache_hit_rate: ~same
Nia: steady KV hitrate suggests not cache invalidation, likely hotter CPU in proto/serialization or extra work in batch flush decisions.
Omar: grabbed a sampling flamegraph from host-canary-01:
```
  40%   proto::marshal::serialize_envelope
  18%   runtime::kernel_selector::compute_costs
  12%   batcher::should_flush
   8%   http::sse::buffer_flush
  22%   other
```
Omar: serialize_envelope spike stands out. The new envelope wraps tool metadata and currently does a synchronous JSON conversion when tool-calls exist.
Kai: that JSON conversion was added to make downstream tooling easier, but doing it inline on the hot path was questionable.
Avery: local repro command: `./scripts/bench_stream --concurrency 6 --samples 2000 --toolcalls=on`
Avery: before the envelope change:
```
p95=52ms
serialize_median=5.1ms
```
Avery: after the change:
```
p95=88ms
serialize_median=17.9ms
```
Nia: big delta. Does kernel_selector change also pick different kernels causing extra latency? Could be compounded.
Omar: quick isolation test — toggled runtime.flags.kernel_cost_model=false on one canary host. No meaningful change to the spike; serialize still hot.
Kai: so primary cause is sync JSON marshal in proto path. Potential mitigations:
  1) revert the envelope change (fastest, obvious rollback)
  2) short-circuit: only run JSON marshal when tool metadata present (cheap guard)
  3) move JSON marshal to async worker / off-net thread and attach pointer to response later (more complex)
Avery: I can prototype the short-circuit guard in ~90m and run perf CI.
BenchBot: queued perf CI run for short-circuit branch. Expected improvement: p95 -30ms if serialize becomes cheap again.
DeployBot: paused remaining canaries at 17:58, rollout flagged: perf/regression.
Avery: temporary mitigation plan: apply short-circuit guard + enable kernel telemetry. If perf CI shows p95 recovery, unpause and gradually resume. Otherwise revert.
Nia: note for postmortem: add a perf CI smoke test that runs a small streaming workload whenever proto or streaming framing code changes.
Omar: results from perf CI (short-circuit): serialize_median=5.9ms, p95 back to ~56ms. Microbench logs: ci.internal/reports/stream_shortcircuit_1805.
Kai: good. I'll open a follow-up to move JSON marshal off the hot path properly and add an opt-in flag for the envelope format. Also add a guardrail in PR review checklist about synchronous serialization in request/response hot paths.
Avery: opening revert PR as a fallback, but hold for now.
BenchBot: CI for revert PR queued but marked low priority.
DeployBot: canary remains paused until we validate kernel telemetry.
Nia: action items:
  - Avery: land short-circuit patch + perf CI (ETA ~2h)
  - Kai: follow-up PR to async marshal and flag (ETA next week)
  - Omar: add streaming smoke to perf CI for proto changes (ETA 3 days)
  - BenchBot: post perf deltas in this thread when ready
Avery: thanks everyone. We'll re-run a 1k-sample smoke on the unpaused canary before any resume. Marking P0 for streaming perf until we have a clean canary. :eyes:
